title: GDP 怎么算
lead: 同一笔经济活动，可以从生产、收入、支出三个方向加总，结果必然相等。
leadEn: The same activity can be added up from production, income or expenditure — and the totals must match.

points.v: 各行业增加值之和＝总产出 − 中间投入，避免重复计算。
points.vEn: Sum of value added = gross output minus intermediate inputs, avoiding double counting.

points.v: 工资 + 利息 + 租金 + 利润 + 生产税净额，即各种要素拿到手的收入。
points.vEn: Wages + interest + rent + profit + net taxes on production: what factors of production receive.

points.v: C + I + G + NX，即消费、投资、政府支出与净出口。
points.vEn: C + I + G + NX: consumption, investment, government spending and net exports.

points.v: 名义 GDP 用当期价格，实际 GDP 剔除物价变动，比较不同年份必须用实际值。
points.vEn: Nominal GDP uses current prices; real GDP strips out price changes and is the right basis for comparison.

watch: GDP 不统计家务劳动与志愿服务，也不扣除环境损耗，因此「增长」并不自动等于「变好」。
人均 GDP 上升而中位数收入停滞，说明增长成果集中，需另看分配数据。
watchEn: GDP excludes unpaid household work and volunteer activity, and does not deduct environmental damage, so growth is not automatically wellbeing.
Rising GDP per capita with stagnant median income means gains are concentrated; distribution data are needed.

sources.label: 联合国 SNA 2008 国民账户体系

title: 通胀从哪来
lead: 需求过旺、成本上升、货币过多与预期自我实现，是四条主要路径。
leadEn: Excess demand, rising costs, too much money and self-fulfilling expectations are the four main routes.

points.v: 总需求超过潜在产出，买家竞价推高价格。
points.vEn: Aggregate demand exceeds potential output, and buyers bid prices up.

points.v: 能源、原料、工资或汇率变动抬高生产成本，企业转嫁至售价。
points.vEn: Energy, input, wage or exchange-rate shocks raise costs, which firms pass on.

points.v: 货币与信贷增速长期远超产出增速，最终表现为物价上涨。
points.vEn: Money and credit growing far faster than output eventually shows up in prices.

points.v: 当人人预期涨价，就会提前囤货、要求加薪，把预期变成现实。
points.vEn: When everyone expects higher prices, they stock up and demand raises, turning expectation into fact.

watch: 「通胀都是货币超发」是过度简化：供给冲击也能在货币稳定时推高物价。
核心通胀（剔除能源与食品）更能反映趋势，因为其波动小、粘性强。
watchEn: 'Inflation is always just money printing' oversimplifies: supply shocks can raise prices even with stable money.
Core inflation (excluding energy and food) tracks the trend better because it is less volatile and more persistent.

sources.label: IMF《世界经济展望》通胀章节
sources.labelEn: IMF World Economic Outlook, inflation chapter

title: 货币政策如何传导
lead: 央行只调一个政策利率，效果却要经过银行、资产价格、汇率与预期四条渠道才能到达实体。
leadEn: The central bank moves one policy rate, but the effect reaches the real economy through four channels.

points.v: 政策利率影响贷款与存款利率，进而影响投资与消费意愿。
points.vEn: The policy rate moves lending and deposit rates, shaping investment and consumption.

points.v: 利率下降抬高股票与房产估值，通过财富效应刺激支出。
points.vEn: Lower rates lift equity and property valuations, and wealth effects boost spending.

points.v: 银行的风险偏好与资本状况决定信贷能不能顺利投放。
points.vEn: Bank risk appetite and capital determine whether credit actually flows.

points.v: 加息吸引资金流入、本币升值，进而影响出口竞争力。
points.vEn: Higher rates attract capital, appreciate the currency and affect export competitiveness.

watch: 传导有滞后，通常需要几个季度才见效，所以政策要看前瞻而非当下数据。
当利率接近零、银行不愿放贷时，常规工具失效，需要非常规手段。
watchEn: Transmission lags by quarters, so policy should respond to the outlook rather than today's data.
Near zero rates with reluctant banks break conventional tools, requiring unconventional ones.

sources.label: BIS 货币政策传导机制研究
sources.labelEn: BIS research on monetary policy transmission

title: 财政政策的乘数与局限
lead: 政府多花一块钱，最终可能带动超过一块钱的产出，也可能被挤出私人支出而所剩无几。
leadEn: One unit of government spending may generate more than one unit of output — or crowd out private spending and achieve little.

points.v: 支出变成他人收入，再被花掉，形成连锁反应，总效果大于初始金额。
points.vEn: Spending becomes someone's income, which is spent again, so the total exceeds the initial amount.

points.v: 政府大量借债推高利率，可能压缩私人投资。
points.vEn: Heavy government borrowing can push rates up and displace private investment.

points.v: 累进税与失业救济在经济下行时自动扩大支出、上行时自动收缩。
points.vEn: Progressive taxes and unemployment benefits expand automatically in downturns and contract in booms.

points.v: 识别、决策、执行三重时滞，加上项目质量差异，决定最终效果。
points.vEn: Recognition, decision and implementation lags, plus project quality, determine the outcome.

watch: 乘数大小高度依赖经济是否已有闲置产能：满负荷时刺激多变成涨价。
长期看财政可持续性受债务利息负担约束，短期刺激与长期偿债需要权衡。
watchEn: Multipliers depend on slack: near full capacity, stimulus mostly becomes inflation.
Fiscal sustainability is bound by debt service, so short-run stimulus trades off against long-run repayment.

title: 失业的三种类型
lead: 摩擦性、结构性、周期性失业的成因不同，对应政策也完全不同。
leadEn: Frictional, structural and cyclical unemployment have different causes and need different policies.

points.v: 换工作、找工作需要时间，属于正常的市场匹配过程。
points.vEn: Time needed to search and switch jobs: a normal matching process.

points.v: 技术或产业变迁使技能与岗位错配，短期刺激无法解决。
points.vEn: Technology or industry shifts mismatch skills and vacancies; demand stimulus cannot fix it.

points.v: 总需求不足导致企业裁员，需要财政与货币宽松来修复。
points.vEn: Weak aggregate demand causes layoffs; fiscal and monetary easing is the remedy.

points.v: 即使经济正常运转也会存在的失业水平，由摩擦与结构因素决定。
points.vEn: The unemployment level that persists even in a healthy economy, set by frictional and structural factors.

watch: 失业率下降可能只是因为人们放弃找工作退出劳动力，需同时看劳动参与率。
青年失业与长期失业的代价最高，因为技能与信心会随时间流失。
watchEn: A falling unemployment rate can simply reflect people leaving the labour force; watch participation too.
Youth and long-term unemployment are the costliest as skills and confidence erode.

sources.label: ILO 就业与失业统计口径
sources.labelEn: ILO definitions of employment and unemployment

title: 经济周期
lead: 扩张与收缩交替出现，幅度与持续时间并不规则，但机制有几条常见线索。
leadEn: Expansions and contractions alternate irregularly, yet a few mechanisms recur.

points.v: 宽松时加杠杆推高资产价格，收紧时去杠杆放大下行。
points.vEn: Easy money leverages up asset prices; tightening deleverages and amplifies the downturn.

points.v: 企业补库存与去库存的交替，短周期波动的主要来源。
points.vEn: Alternating inventory building and destocking drives short cycles.

points.v: 重大技术或基础设施投资形成多年一轮的荣枯。
points.vEn: Major technology or infrastructure waves create multi-year booms and busts.

points.v: 逆周期调控可以平滑波动，也可能延后调整、积累风险。
points.vEn: Countercyclical policy can smooth swings, or delay adjustment and build risk.

watch: 「周期可预测」的说法常被高估：转折点的精确定时几乎无人能持续做到。
平稳期越长，参与者越容易低估风险，杠杆与期限错配往往在此时积累。
watchEn: Claims that cycles are predictable are usually overstated: nobody reliably times turning points.
The longer the calm, the more risk is underestimated, and leverage and maturity mismatch accumulate.
